rituals.title: MAKE THE BELIEF BET
rituals.goal: Let one behaviour test what argument cannot settle.
rituals.steps:
1. State Belief — State the belief as a clear prediction.
2. Choose Safe — Choose a safe, small action that could prove it wrong as well as right.
3. Picture Outcome — Hold the expected result before acting.
4. Test Observation — Run the test, then compare observation with prediction.
5. Pay Out — Pay out only to evidence.
rituals.win: ✓ Evidence won the bet. Belief did not get a sympathy payout.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Pay Out”; release the score.
• Pulled back? Touch “Picture Outcome”.
• “Test Observation” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “State Belief” versus “Pay Out”: what eased?
• I can use “Choose Safe” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: State Belief → Choose Safe → Picture Outcome → Test Observation → Pay Out
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Cancel any experiment involving danger, coercion, medical risk, or another person’s consent.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
rituals.goal: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.steps:
1. Name — Name five versions of the task from almost easy to really stretching.
2. Cross Out — Remove the zero-effort decoy.
3. Remain Version — Do the smallest remaining version that leaves visible evidence—one paragraph, one call, one plate washed.
4. Climb Stair — Next time, climb only one stair.
rituals.win: ✓ One stair was enough to create movement.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Climb Stair”; release the score.
• On return, repeat “Remain Version”.
• “Remain Version” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Name” → “Climb Stair”?
• I can use “Cross Out” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Name → Cross Out → Remain Version → Climb Stair
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Reduce the step further if illness, exhaustion, or overload is being ignored.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MOOD HAS ALIBIS
rituals.goal: Test what the day does to the feeling.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Activity — Choose one activity.
2. Score Expected — Before it, score expected mood; at the start, notice your actual mood; at the end, score again.
3. Add Sentence — Add one sentence about what changed during the activity.
4. Try Three Ways — Repeat with three different actions before deciding ‘nothing helps.’
rituals.win: ✓ The feeling kept its voice but lost the judge’s chair.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Try Three Ways”; let feeling settle.
• Re-entry move: “Add Sentence”.
• “Add Sentence” separates feeling from fact.
• “Choose Activity” → “Try Three Ways”: what changed?
• I can use “Score Expected” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Activity → Score Expected → Add Sentence → Try Three Ways
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek professional support if low mood is severe, persistent, or linked to self-harm thoughts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TWO ENGINES
rituals.goal: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.steps:
1. Schedule Chosen — For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence.
2. Make Small — Make both small enough to happen.
3. Check Both — After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only.
4. Drop Demand — Do not demand that either activity fix everything.
rituals.win: ✓ Good-enough became usable again.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Drop Demand”; release the score.
• If it flares, choose “Check Both”.
• “Check Both” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Drop Demand”: what changed from “Schedule Chosen”?
• I can use “Make Small” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Schedule Chosen → Make Small → Check Both → Drop Demand
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Rebalance if achievement becomes punishment or pleasure becomes avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
rituals.goal: Your environment casts ballots before willpower arrives.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick Desired — Pick one desired behaviour and one unwanted default.
2. Place Object — Place the first object needed for the desired action directly in your path.
3. Add Deliberate — Add one small obstacle to the unwanted route: distance, logout, container, timer, or removal.
4. Let Space Vote — Let the room make the better vote easier.
rituals.win: ✓ The room tipped the vote toward the choice I actually want.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Space Vote”; release the score.
• Re-entry move: “Add Deliberate”.
• “Add Deliberate” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Pick Desired” to “Let Space Vote”: what loosened?
• I can use “Place Object” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Pick Desired → Place Object → Add Deliberate → Let Space Vote
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep changes reversible and never block access to medication, food, safety, or essential contact.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
rituals.goal: The ritual expects you; do not show up.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Cue — Name the cue and the usual calming act it normally summons.
2. Contact — Contact only a manageable dose of the cue.
3. Keep Hands — Keep your hands and attention out of the ritual while the urge changes on its own.
4. Mark Peak — Hold the peak and the first natural drop.
5. Let Learning Land — The learning comes from not doing the old ritual.
rituals.win: ✓ The urge stayed loud without taking the wheel.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Learning Land”; let wanting crest.
• Skip replay; use “Keep Hands”.
• “Mark Peak” keeps wanting off controls.
• Compare “Name Cue” with “Let Learning Land”.
• I can use “Contact” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Cue → Contact → Keep Hands → Mark Peak → Let Learning Land
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use clinical guidance for severe OCD, addiction, eating disorders, or exposures that feel unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BODY VETO
rituals.goal: Install a movement the habit cannot do beside.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Motor — Spot the first motor cue—reaching, picking, scrolling, biting, clenching.
2. Choose Safe — Use a safe opposite posture and practise it slowly three times.
3. Enter Posture — When the cue appears, enter that posture for ten seconds while naming the urge.
4. Decide Consciously — Then decide consciously.
rituals.win: ✓ Habit vetoed. The choice came back online.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Decide Consciously”; let wanting crest.
• Restart detected: “Enter Posture”.
• “Enter Posture” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Decide Consciously”: what changed from “Identify Motor”?
• I can use “Choose Safe” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Motor → Choose Safe → Enter Posture → Decide Consciously
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Choose another response if the posture causes pain, strain, or social risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHEN/THEN FIRMWARE
rituals.goal: Pre-decide the moment that usually steals the decision.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Line — Picture one line only: WHEN [specific visible cue], THEN I WILL [small physical action].
2. Remove Vague — Remove vague words such as try, soon, or better.
3. Imagine Cue — Imagine the cue once, do the action once, and place the rule where the cue occurs.
4. Skip Pep Talk — Skip the pep talk.
rituals.win: ✓ Decision installed before motivation had a chance to bargain.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Skip Pep Talk”; slow the clock.
• Skip replay; use “Imagine Cue”.
• “Imagine Cue” puts facts above speed.
• “Picture Line” to “Skip Pep Talk”: what loosened?
• I can use “Remove Vague” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Line → Remove Vague → Imagine Cue → Skip Pep Talk
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Rewrite the rule if the trigger is unclear or the response depends on another person.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE FIRST DRIFT
rituals.goal: Relapse announces itself quietly before it becomes a return.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the Path — Trace the unwanted behaviour backward in your mind: first act, private permission, routine change, environment shift, body state.
2. Mark Earliest — Place a red dot on the earliest sign you could realistically notice.
3. Plant Interrupt — Attach one simple interruption to that red dot and rehearse what you will do when it appears.
rituals.win: ✓ I found the drift point before the whole slide began.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Plant Interrupt”; no forcing.
• Return once to “Mark Earliest”.
• “Mark Earliest” keeps sensation as data.
• “Picture the Path” → “Plant Interrupt”: what changed?
• I can use “Mark Earliest” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture the Path → Mark Earliest → Tell Support
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
For substance withdrawal, overdose risk, or dangerous relapse, use medical and emergency support rather than self-management alone.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
rituals.goal: An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.
rituals.steps:
1. Level — Notice its current level and where it moves in the body.
2. Watch Slope — Watch for slope: rising, flattening, cresting, falling.
3. Imagine Urge — Every thirty seconds, imagine the next point without acting on the urge.
4. Name Change — When the line changes direction, name the change.
5. Choose Time — Choose what protects the next hour.
rituals.win: ✓ The craving curved; the next hour kept the vote.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Time”; let wanting crest.
• Re-entry move: “Imagine Urge”.
• “Name Change” keeps wanting off controls.
• What lost power: “Level” → “Choose Time”?
• I can use “Watch Slope” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Level → Watch Slope → Imagine Urge → Name Change → Choose Time
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Cravings linked to withdrawal, overdose, or medical danger require professional help.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ONE VISIBLE VOTE
rituals.goal: Values become real only after the body votes.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Value — Choose a value and design its smallest public evidence: send the honest line, open the document, place the medicine beside water, step outside for two minutes.
2. Complete Shift — Complete it before upgrading the plan.
3. Cast Tiny Vote — A tiny enacted vote outranks a perfect private speech.
rituals.win: ✓ Made one tiny value-vote visible instead of keeping it private.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Cast Tiny Vote”; release the score.
• Loop back? Use “Complete Shift”.
• “Complete Shift” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Look back: “Choose Value” → “Cast Tiny Vote”.
• I can use “Complete Shift” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Value → Complete Shift → Cast Tiny Vote
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Scale down without shame if the action exceeds current capacity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: OBJECTIVE OVER EGO
rituals.goal: The best move may not be the most satisfying proof.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Real — Picture the real objective in seven words or fewer.
2. Name — Name the action that advances it and the action that merely wins, punishes, impresses, or avoids embarrassment.
3. Imagine Tomorrow — Imagine tomorrow’s result after each.
4. Select Works — Select what works, even if the ego receives no trophy.
rituals.win: ✓ The picture widened beyond the selected facts.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Select Works”; slow the clock.
• Re-entry move: “Imagine Tomorrow”.
• “Imagine Tomorrow” puts facts above speed.
• “Picture Real” versus “Select Works”: what eased?
• I can use “Name” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Real → Name → Imagine Tomorrow → Select Works
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Revisit the objective if it excludes dignity, consent, or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: COOL THE ALARM PANEL
rituals.goal: Temperature can reach body alarm before language does.
rituals.steps:
1. Use Cool — Use cool—not painfully cold—water or a wrapped cool pack on the cheeks and around the eyes for a brief interval.
2. Slow — Slow your body while the sensation lands.
3. Remove Name — Remove it, name the room, and reassess the next safe action.
4. End the Cool — Treat the cool sensation as a reset cue. Stop before it becomes an endurance test.
rituals.win: ✓ The alarm cooled without turning discomfort into a test.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “End the Cool”; no breath-holding.
• Loop back? Use “Remove Name”.
• “Remove Name” — alarm isn’t command.
• “End the Cool”: what changed from “Use Cool”?
• I can use “Slow” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Use Cool → Slow → Remove Name → End the Cool
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid with medical contraindications; never use ice directly or hold your breath.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BURN THE EXCESS CHARGE
rituals.goal: Give body alarm a finish line.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Burst — Choose a contained burst: fast stairs, wall pushes, brisk marching, or another safe vigorous movement.
2. Set Short — Set a short timer before starting.
3. End Completely — When it ends, stop completely, feel the after-pulse, and drink water.
4. Let Body — Let the body spend energy without spending your future.
rituals.win: ✓ Panic became a wave with surroundings around it.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Body”; no breath-holding.
• Restart detected: “End Completely”.
• “End Completely” — alarm isn’t command.
• “Choose Burst” → “Let Body”: what changed?
• I can use “Set Short” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Burst → Set Short → End Completely → Let Body
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not attempt intense movement with injury, illness, pregnancy concerns, or medical restrictions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE LONGER OUT-BREATH
rituals.goal: Make urgency leave through a gentler exit.
rituals.steps:
1. Breathe Pulling — Breathe in without pulling extra air.
2. Let Outflow — Let the outflow last slightly longer, as though fogging a distant window silently.
3. Repeat Comfortable — Repeat only while comfortable; keep shoulders quiet and jaw loose.
4. Breathe Workable — After several rounds, resume natural breathing and look for one workable decision.
rituals.win: ✓ The craving lost its automatic route to action.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Breathe Workable”; slow the clock.
• Catch restart with “Repeat Comfortable”.
• “Repeat Comfortable” puts facts above speed.
• Before/after: “Breathe Pulling” → “Breathe Workable”.
• I can use “Let Outflow” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Breathe Pulling → Let Outflow → Repeat Comfortable → Breathe Workable
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Return to ordinary breathing immediately if light-headed, air-hungry, or panicky.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: STAY FOR THE UPDATE
rituals.goal: Safe contact gives fear new data.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose External — Choose an external cue low enough on your fear ladder to approach voluntarily.
2. Enter Escape — Enter without escape and remain until you observe at least one mismatch between prediction and reality.
3. Name Mismatch — Name the mismatch before leaving.
4. Repeat Later — Repeat later under safe conditions rather than chasing maximum distress.
rituals.win: ✓ The future reopened beyond the alarm.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Repeat Later”; leave the forecast.
• Restart detected: “Name Mismatch”.
• “Name Mismatch” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Repeat Later”: what changed from “Choose External”?
• I can use “Enter Escape” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose External → Enter Escape → Name Mismatch → Repeat Later
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Exposure needs clinical support when trauma, medical risk, severe phobia, or feeling unreal or disconnected is involved.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE CONTROLLED REPLAY
rituals.goal: A feared scene needs a container, not a flood.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Time — Set a start time, endpoint, grounding object, and recovery plan.
2. Recount — Recount or visualise the feared scene at a manageable pace without changing key facts.
3. Prediction — Notice shifts in prediction or emotion across the telling.
4. Finish Location — Finish by naming present location and date.
rituals.win: ✓ Replay closed in the present: current place, current date, current choice.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Location”; notice the room.
• Catch restart with “Prediction”.
• “Prediction” proves the present returned.
• Before/after: “Set Time” → “Finish Location”.
• I can use “Recount” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Set Time → Recount → Prediction → Finish Location
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not self-administer for severe trauma, psychosis, acute crisis, or destabilising memories.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LEAVE ONE QUESTION OPEN
rituals.goal: Uncertainty can remain unfinished without becoming an emergency.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Low — Choose a low-stakes unknown.
2. Picture Card — Picture it on a card and forbid checking, asking, or mentally solving until a set time.
3. Carry Unanswered — Carry the unanswered card while doing normal life.
4. Watch The Urge — At review, notice what the urge did—not whether certainty arrived.
rituals.win: ✓ The unanswered part stopped demanding immediate closure.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Watch The Urge”; leave it unanswered.
• Use “Carry Unanswered” on return.
• “Carry Unanswered” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Choose Low” → “Watch The Urge”: what changed?
• I can use “Picture Card” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Low → Picture Card → Carry Unanswered → Watch The Urge
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Begin with smaller unknowns if abstaining causes overwhelming distress.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
rituals.goal: Stay long enough to learn what happens after the peak.
rituals.steps:
1. Highest — During a safe practice round, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
2. Stay Past Relief — Do not leave at that first relief.
3. Remain Cue — Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
4. Leave After Recovery — Departure follows learning, not panic.
rituals.win: ✓ Exit came after recovery—not at panic’s command.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Leave After Recovery”; no breath-holding.
• On return: “Remain Cue”.
• “Remain Cue” — alarm isn’t command.
• “Highest” → “Leave After Recovery”: what changed?
• I can use “Stay Past Relief” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Highest → Stay Past Relief → Remain Cue → Leave After Recovery
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Leave immediately if circumstances become genuinely unsafe or sense of where you are deteriorates.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: REMOVE ONE INVISIBLE CRUTCH
rituals.goal: A crutch can hide the safety already holding you.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Protective — During a manageable practice round, spot one protective act that is unnecessary: gripping, rehearsing, sitting by the exit, checking pulse, carrying extra certainty.
2. Drop Legitimate — Drop only that act while keeping legitimate safety intact.
3. Observe Outcome — Observe what the outcome says without it.
rituals.win: ✓ Pressure separated from importance.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Observe Outcome”; slow the clock.
• Pulled back? Touch “Drop Legitimate”.
• “Drop Legitimate” puts facts above speed.
• What lost power: “Identify Protective” → “Observe Outcome”?
• I can use “Drop Legitimate” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Protective → Drop Legitimate → Observe Outcome
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Never remove medically required or genuinely protective behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MOVE THE LESSON
rituals.goal: Learning that works in one room may not travel by itself.
rituals.steps:
1. Repeat Mastered — Repeat a mastered practice while changing one feature: location, time, cue order, duration, or intensity.
2. Change Again — On the next round, alter a different feature.
3. Map Transfer — Keep a small mental map of where the skill still works.
4. Make Portable — Let variation turn a local success into portable knowledge.
rituals.win: ✓ The lesson travelled. It no longer belongs to one room.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Make Portable”; keep both sides.
• Use “Map Transfer” on return.
• “Map Transfer” widens the evidence field.
• At “Make Portable”, compare “Repeat Mastered”.
• I can use “Change Again” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Repeat Mastered → Round → Keep Small → Turn Local
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Vary only within the established safe range.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE TWO-CUE MERGE
rituals.goal: Combine mastered signals only after each can stand alone.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Triggers — Select two triggers already manageable separately.
2. Predict Joining — Predict what joining them will add.
3. Drop Unnecessary — Contact both at a modest dose while dropping unnecessary escape.
4. Stay Long — Stay long enough to compare the combined result with the prediction, then recover fully.
rituals.win: ✓ Fear kept a warning, not a prophecy.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Stay Long”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Drop Unnecessary”.
• “Drop Unnecessary” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Select Triggers” → “Stay Long”: what changed?
• I can use “Predict Joining” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Select Triggers → Predict Joining → Drop Unnecessary → Stay Long
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not compound unmastered trauma cues or exceed the planned tolerance range.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TAKE SAFETY ON TOUR
rituals.goal: A lesson becomes reliable when the address changes.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Safe — Pick a different secure setting for a skill already learned elsewhere.
2. Enter Earlier — Before entering, recall the earlier evidence in one sentence.
3. Practise Transfers — Practise, notice what transfers, and spot any context-specific obstacle.
4. Leave Local — Leave with a local reminder for next time.
rituals.win: ✓ The evidence field stopped being edited by one conclusion.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Leave Local”; keep both sides.
• Shortcut: “Practise Transfers”, once.
• “Practise Transfers” widens the evidence field.
• What lost power: “Choose Safe” → “Leave Local”?
• I can use “Enter Earlier” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Safe → Enter Earlier → Practise Transfers → Leave Local
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use supported settings when unfamiliar places create major risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TURN UP THE WHISPER
rituals.goal: A tiny movement may be the body’s unfinished instruction.
rituals.steps:
1. Smallest — Notice the smallest spontaneous tendency: sway, curl, stretch, turn, reach.
2. Pause Enlarge — Enlarge it by only ten percent and pause.
3. Ask Whether — Check if it brings ease, protection, energy, or nothing.
4. Let Determine — Let the answer determine whether to continue, reverse, or stop.
rituals.win: ✓ The whisper became clear enough to guide the next choice.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Determine”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Ask Whether”, once.
• “Ask Whether” keeps sensation as data.
• “Smallest” → “Let Determine”: what changed?
• I can use “Pause Enlarge” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Smallest → Pause Enlarge → Ask Whether → Let Determine
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep amplitude small around pain, injury, or unstable balance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT
rituals.goal: Give the body proof that time has moved.
rituals.steps:
1. Say Age — Say the full date, your current age, location, and who is here.
2. Name Differences — Name three differences between now and the remembered danger: exits, resources, authority, distance, or choice.
3. State Belongs — Touch one present object while stating, ‘This object belongs to the present.’
rituals.win: ✓ The mind returned from elsewhere without needing a perfect landing.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “State Belongs”; orient to now.
• Shortcut: “Name Differences”, once.
• “Name Differences” moves memory toward then.
• “Say Age” → “State Belongs”: what changed?
• I can use “Name Differences” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Say Age → Name Differences → State Belongs
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use immediate professional help if you cannot regain sense of where you are or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FEAR WITHOUT THE MOVIE
rituals.goal: At the peak, meet energy before narrative claims it.
rituals.steps:
1. Locate Most — If safely steady, locate the most intense fear sensation and say only its movement, charge, heat, and boundary.
2. Remove Prediction — Remove prediction briefly.
3. Keep Hand — Keep one hand or gaze anchored in the room.
4. Let Raw — Let raw body alarm be observed without following its film script.
rituals.win: ✓ Fear became body energy before it could become a movie.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Raw”; then keep moving.
• Restart detected: “Keep Hand”.
• “Keep Hand” proves motion is available.
• “Locate Most” → “Let Raw”: what changed?
• I can use “Remove Prediction” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Locate Most → Remove Prediction → Keep Hand → Let Raw
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not attempt at overwhelming intensity, active danger, or trauma flooding.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: STUDY THE REACTION, NOT THE CHARACTER
rituals.goal: Self-inquiry works better as disciplined research.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Recurring — Choose a reaction that happens often and remember three times it happened.
2. Read Pattern — For each time, notice the trigger, meaning, body feeling, action, and result.
3. Compare Trusted — Compare the three examples with a trusted idea or guide.
4. Test One Guess — Choose one idea to test. Leave your whole character out of the experiment.
rituals.win: ✓ One reaction became a testable clue, not a character verdict.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Test One Guess”; no forcing.
• Use “Compare Trusted” on return.
• “Compare Trusted” keeps sensation as data.
• At “Test One Guess”, compare “Choose Recurring”.
• I can use “Read Pattern” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Recurring → Read Pattern → Compare Trusted → Test One Guess
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Pause study when reflection becomes self-surveillance or shame.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHAT REMAINS WHEN REWARD LEAVES?
rituals.goal: Duty becomes clearer after fear and praise exit the room.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Role — Name your role, the people affected, and the values governing it.
2. Remove Applause — Mentally remove applause, punishment, and personal advantage.
3. Ask Responsibility — Ask which responsibility still stands.
4. Set Role Limit — Convert that answer into a time-bound action and one limit on what the role does not require.
rituals.win: ✓ The reward disappeared; the part I still cared about stayed.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Set Role Limit”; keep the compass.
• If it flares, choose “Ask Responsibility”.
• “Ask Responsibility” keeps meaning in motion.

rituals.goal: Must-have limits should shape the field before desire fills it.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Safety — Picture safety, ethics, consent, resources, and timing constraints first.
2. Eliminate — Eliminate choices that violate them.
3. Generate — Generate options only inside the surviving space.
4. Lead With Constraints — Treat creativity as solving within reality, not arguing with the boundary.
rituals.win: ✓ I let the constraints shape the field before the options started campaigning.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Lead With Constraints”; release extra load.
• On return, repeat “Generate”.
• “Generate” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• At “Lead With Constraints”, compare “Picture Safety”.
• I can use “Eliminate” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Safety → Eliminate → Generate → Lead With Constraints
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Challenge assumed constraints that lack factual support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
